sources.entry: SSH Tunnel Manager - Menu bar app for managing SSH port forwards (local, remote, SOCKS, jump host) that auto-reconnects when the connection drops.

summary.one_liner: A lightweight macOS menu bar app written in native Swift/AppKit for managing SSH port forwards (local, remote, SOCKS, jump host) with auto-reconnect.
keywords: open source alternative to core tunnel
summary.what_it_does: The app runs in the macOS menu bar and lets you configure SSH tunnels once and toggle them on or off with one click. Each tunnel can hold multiple port mappings over one SSH connection, including local (-L), remote (-R), and dynamic SOCKS (-D) forwards. A jump host option adds -J so you can reach a host behind one or more bastions. Tunnels auto-reconnect when they drop, and failed or dropped tunnels display a reason such as auth failure, refused, unreachable, DNS, changed host key, or port in use. The README also covers per-tunnel options (ConnectTimeout, keepalive, compression, host-key handling, extra ssh flags), sound and notification alerts, a port-conflict guard, and reuse of ~/.ssh/config aliases. It uses the system SSH binary and stores config in a JSON file under Application Support.
use_cases: keep a database tunnel to a remote server running
reach internal services through a bastion host
run a SOCKS proxy into a private network
expose a local dev server through a public server
auto-reconnect SSH port forwards after sleep or network drops
manage many ssh -L tunnels from the menu bar
notable: Native Swift/AppKit with no Electron and no bundled SSH binaries; uses system ssh
Supports local, remote, and SOCKS forwards mixed within one tunnel, plus multi-hop jump host chains
Failure reasons shown in the menu bar and detail view, not just 'disconnected'
Port-conflict guard prevents two tunnels from claiming the same local port
Config stored as JSON at ~/Library/Application Support/SSHTunnelManager/tunnels.json
caveats: Requires macOS 14+ and Xcode 15+ to build from source
The app is not notarized; first launch needs right-click Open or a quarantine-clearing command
Remote forwards bound to 0.0.0.0 need GatewayPorts yes in the server's sshd_config
Skip host key check option disables host-key verification and is insecure
